title: Gado-Gado (Indonesian Vegetable Salad with Peanut Sauce)
summary: Boiled potatoes, blanched cabbage, green beans and bean sprouts with fried tofu, cucumber, tomato and hard-boiled egg, served with a peanut sauce of shallot, garlic, chilli, palm sugar, tamarind and kecap manis.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm pieces
green beans, cut into 5 cm lengths
fried tofu puffs, cut into 3 cm pieces

steps.title: Make the peanut sauce
steps.text: Grind the peanuts in the food processor to a coarse, sandy paste and set aside. Blitz the shallots, garlic, chillies, sugar and salt to a rough paste. Simmer the water and tamarind in the small pan for 3 min, then stir in both pastes and the kecap manis and simmer for 5-6 min, stirring often so it does not catch, until thick and creamy. Add the lime juice and loosen with a splash of water if needed.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 min so the yolks are fully set, then chill in iced water, peel and quarter.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in the same pan for 8-10 min until tender and drain. Blanch the cabbage for 1 min, the green beans for 2 min and the bean sprouts for 20 seconds, chilling each in the iced water and draining on paper. Chilling keeps them bright and crisp.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Arrange the vegetables, tofu, cucumber, tomato and eggs on the platter and spoon over the warm peanut sauce, or serve it alongside.

tips: Smooth or crunchy natural peanut butter (about 150 g) can replace the ground peanuts.
Add a little shrimp paste to the chilli paste for a more traditional depth; note that it adds crustaceans.
Prawn crackers and crisp fried shallots are classic on top.
storage: Store the components separately, refrigerated, up to 2 days. The peanut sauce keeps 5 days; reheat gently with a splash of water, until steaming (74 °C) if serving warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
